subject: Clearline: alleged EU availability gap during rolling deploy — request to verify and propose remedy
messages:
From: Nathan Cole <nathan@clearline.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Clearline Accounts <accounting@clearline.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Unexpected availability gap impacting checkout (Clearline) — request for SLA reconciliation

Kim,

We saw a sustained availability gap yesterday evening during our EU checkout peak and need Redwood to confirm the window for SLA reconciliation and next steps. Summary below: 

- Impact window (observed): 2028-07-03 22:33:14 UTC → 2028-07-03 22:51:06 UTC (~17m52s)
- Symptom: 503 responses and increased retries across our checkout flow; ~2% of transactions failed end-to-end during the window.
- Customer impact: multi-tenant checkout outages for several European customers (IDs attached).

I've attached a screenshot of our monitoring and a sample list of affected request IDs (sample_event_ids.txt). Please confirm: 1) whether Redwood observed a matching service availability window in eu-west-1, 2) whether this meets SLA eligibility for a credit, and 3) when we can expect a postmortem.

We rely on the committed uptime for Clearline's EU traffic during business hours; this outage materially affected revenue. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Nathan Cole

Kim,

I've finished the initial telemetry sweep and pulled the traces you asked for. Summary: 

- Confirmation: we observed a sustained degradation in eu-west-1 that matches Clearline's reported window. Our synthetic and ingestion traces show a spike in 503s between 2028-07-03 22:33:10 UTC and 2028-07-03 22:51:28 UTC (~18m18s).
- Root cause (short): an automated canary deploy in eu-west-1 triggered an unexpected autoscaler hot-loop as a new kernel path was exercised; this caused rapid instance churn and a routing fallback that delivered 503s for warmup/dead instances.
- Evidence: raw trace bundle and scheduler logs uploaded to S3 (drive link below). Key artifacts: eu-west-1-deploy-traces-0703.tar.gz, scheduler-eventlog-0703.ndjson.

SLA impact and preliminary credit calc: per our SLA, we consider sustained unavailability >10 minutes for regional production tiers eligible for proportional credit. For Clearline's committed tier, the proportional remedy would be calculated over the impacted window. Rough estimate: 18.3 minutes → qualifies. Proposed initial credit: 10% service-month prorated over the impacted minute fraction (we should run exact minutes against their committed uptime hours — I can produce the formal calculation for billing).

Next steps I propose: 
1) Share the raw bundle with Clearline (sensitive data redacted) and confirm the affected tenant IDs.
2) Schedule a joint postmortem (SRE + Product + Clearline ops) — suggested times next week.
3) Patch the canary rollout gating to prevent autoscaler hot-loop from impacting routing (we'll open RED-4371 to track).

Artifacts & links:
- Evidence bundle (GDrive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-clearline-evidence
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/RED-4371

I've attached the tar.gz (eu-west-1-deploy-traces-0703.tar.gz) to this message for accounting. Let me know if you want me to include a short preliminary credit calc table — I can send it to billing once we confirm tenant hours.

Diego Fernandez
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com
